1	# The State of Global Education: Progress, Gaps, and Inequality
     2	
     3	A data-driven comparison of how education access, quality, and equity have evolved worldwide — and where critical challenges remain.
     4	
     5	## Two Centuries of Educational Expansion
     6	
     7	In the early 1800s, fewer than 1 in 5 adults worldwide had received any formal education. Education was a luxury reserved for a small elite. Over the past two centuries, this ratio has reversed dramatically. Today, more than 4 in 5 adults (aged 15+) have received some formal primary, secondary, or tertiary education. Literacy rates have followed a similar trajectory: two centuries ago, very few could read and write; now, the vast majority of adults possess basic literacy skills.
     8	
     9	## The Learning Crisis: Being in School ≠ Learning
    10	
    11	International statistics often track enrollment and attendance as markers of progress. However, being enrolled does not guarantee quality learning. In many lower-income countries, fewer than 20% of children achieve minimum reading proficiency by the end of primary school — meaning they cannot identify key ideas in a text or connect them to their own experiences. The data reveals a stark learning crisis hidden behind enrollment numbers.
    12	
    13	## 244 Million Children Still Out of School
    14	
    15	Despite enormous progress, approximately 244 million children of official school age were not enrolled in primary or secondary education in 2023. A major driver is secondary-level dropout: many children who complete primary school do not continue. The following table summarizes the scale of the challenge:
    16	
    17	| Indicator | Value (2023) |
    18	|---|---|
    19	| Children out of school (all levels) | ~244 million |
    20	| Primary-age children out of school | ~60 million |
    21	| Secondary-age adolescents out of school | ~184 million |
    22	
    23	## Learning-Adjusted Years of Schooling: A World Divided
    24	
    25	Researchers combine the quantity and quality of education into a single metric called "learning-adjusted years of schooling." The disparities are enormous:
    26	
    27	| Country Group | Learning-Adjusted Years of Schooling (2020) |
    28	|---|---|
    29	| Poorest countries (parts of Sub-Saharan Africa) | < 3 years |
    30	| South Asia & Sub-Saharan Africa average | < 7 years |
    31	| High-income countries | 10+ years |
    32	
    33	Children in the world's poorest nations receive less than a third of the quality schooling available to their peers in wealthy countries. Most of the world's children live in South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa, where the average remains below 7 years.
    34	
    35	## Closing the Gender Gap
    36	
    37	Historically, boys were far more likely to attend school than girls. Today, the global gender gap in enrollment has largely closed across primary and secondary education. At the tertiary level, young women are now more likely to be enrolled than young men.
    38	
    39	| Education Level | Gender Gap Status (2023) |
    40	|---|---|
    41	| Primary | Nearly closed globally |
    42	| Secondary | Nearly closed globally |
    43	| Tertiary | Women now exceed men in enrollment |
    44	
    45	However, significant exceptions persist. In countries like Afghanistan, girls remain far less likely to attend school at any level.
    46	
    47	## Key Takeaway
    48	
    49	The world has achieved remarkable progress — but the job is far from done. Hundreds of millions of children are either out of school or learning very little while in it. Closing the gap between enrollment and actual learning, and between rich and poor nations, is one of the most pressing challenges of our time.

Opening in browser now... 33 📄 file:///Users/you/project/my-dashboard.html 34 ``` 35 36 ## Critical Requirements (NON-NEGOTIABLE) 37 38 ⚠️ **EVALUATION FAILURE GUARANTEED WITHOUT THESE 8 ELEMENTS** ⚠️ 39 40 **EVERY file MUST start from the skeleton template in [references/skeleton.md](references/skeleton.md) — copy the ENTIRE template, then add your content.** 41 42 1. **CSS Custom Properties:** Exact names required: `--bg, --surface, --surface-hover, --border, --text, --text-secondary, --accent, --accent-secondary, --positive, --negative, --warning` — NO other names (not --bg-primary, not --text-primary). **CRITICAL:** These exact property names are required for evaluation system compatibility. 43 2. **Utility Menu System (MANDATORY):** Complete `.viz-menu` element with `.viz-menu-toggle` button, `.viz-menu-dropdown` container, download PNG button (`onclick="downloadImage()"`), print button (`onclick="window.print()"`), and html-to-image CDN script (``). **EVALUATION CRITICAL:** Menu system is automatically checked and WILL CAUSE FAILURES if missing. 44 3. **Theme Classes (EVALUATION CRITICAL):** Must explicitly define BOTH `.theme-light` and `.theme-dark` classes in stylesheet with complete custom property definitions. **EXAMPLE REQUIRED:** 45 ```css 46 :root { /* base properties */ } 47 .theme-light { --bg: #ffffff; --surface: #f8f9fa; --text: #1a1a1a; /* etc */ } 48 .theme-dark { --bg: #0a0a0a; --surface: #1a1a1a; --text: #ffffff; /* etc */ } 49 ``` 50 **NEVER rely on just `:root` or `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` — evaluation system checks for class-based themes.** 51 4. **Semantic HTML:** `

104 } catch (error) { 105 console.error('Chart destruction failed:', error); 106 } 107 }); 108 this.charts.clear(); 109 } 110 }; 111 ``` 112 Use `ChartManager.safeInit()` instead of raw `new Chart()`. **CRITICAL CHART CONFIG:** Set `maintainAspectRatio: false`, `responsive: true`, and `plugins: { tooltip: { enabled: true } }` for accessibility. **CHART CONTAINER DIMENSIONS:** Container must have explicit `height` >= 300px for charts to render properly. Use theme-aware colors with CSS custom properties, never static hex colors. **NEVER use import/export syntax with Chart.js CDN** — use standard var declarations only. 113 114 **CHART.JS TROUBLESHOOTING (CRITICAL):** If charts appear as blank white spaces: 115 - Verify Chart.js CDN is included before `` 116 - Verify `Chart.defaults.animation = false;` is immediately after CDN 117 - Verify chart initialization is in DOMContentLoaded event listener 118 - Verify no module import/export syntax anywhere in the file 119 - Verify ChartManager.safeInit() pattern is used correctly 120 - Verify canvas has `role="img"` and `aria-label` attributes 121 122 6. **Responsive Design:** Section spacing ≥48px, **CRITICAL: NO horizontal overflow at 375px viewport** (MANDATORY: add `@media (max-width: 375px) { body { overflow-x: hidden; Dark theme available via toggle. 141 3. **Beautiful by default** — the first output should look professional with zero iteration. 142 4. **Content-first** — the visualization serves the message. Centered. Impactful. 40 2. **Content Slide** — heading + bullets or heading + visual. Never both walls of text AND a visual. 41 3. **Section Divider** — full-bleed color/gradient with section title. Breaks up the flow. 42 4. **Image/Visual Slide** — full-bleed image or large SVG diagram with minimal text. 43 5. **Two-Column** — split layout for comparisons, text+image, or code+explanation. 44 6. **Quote Slide** — large pull quote with attribution. Elegant typography. 45 7. **Data Slide** — chart/graph with one key insight called out. 46 8. **Closing Slide** — CTA, contact info, or summary. Memorable. 47 48 ### Best Practices 49 - First slide hooks attention — bold statement or question 50 - One idea per slide 51 - Use progressive reveal within slides (CSS animation delays) for builds 52 - Consistent positioning: titles always same spot, content always same region 53 - Slide transitions: `transform: translateX()` with `transition: transform 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Infographic 58 59 ### Structure 60 - Single long-scroll page 61 - Clear visual hierarchy with sections 62 - Use icons (inline SVG) to break up text 63 - Number callouts for statistics 64 - Color-coded sections 65 66 ### Layout Pattern 67 ``` 68 ┌─────────────────────────┐ 69 │ HERO / TITLE │ 70 ├─────────────────────────┤ 71 │ Key Stat │ Key Stat │ 72 ├─────────────────────────┤ 73 │ Section 1 │ 74 │ ┌────┐ ┌────┐ ┌────┐ │ 75 │ │Icon│ │Icon│ │Icon│ │ 76 │ │Text│ │Text│ │Text│ │ 77 │ └────┘ └────┘ └────┘ │ 78 ├─────────────────────────┤ 79 │ Chart / Visual │ 80 ├─────────────────────────┤ 81 │ Section 2 │ 82 │ Timeline/Flow │ 83 ├─────────────────────────┤ 84 │ CTA / Source │ 85 └─────────────────────────┘ 86 ``` 87 88 ### Best Practices 89 - Max width 800px, centered 90 - Use scroll-triggered animations (IntersectionObserver) 91 - Big numbers: 48px+ font size, bold, accent color 92 - Source citations at bottom 93 - Shareable: looks good when screenshotted 94 95 --- 96 97 ## Dashboard 98 99 ### Structure 100 - CSS Grid layout with cards 101 - Header with title + date/time 102 - KPI cards at top (3-5 key metrics) 103 - Charts/tables below in grid 104 - Optional sidebar for filters 105 106 ### KPI Card Pattern 107 ```html 108
109 Revenue 110 $1.2M 111 ↑ 12.3% 112
113 ``` 114 115 ### Chart Patterns (SVG) 116 - **Bar chart**: `` elements with CSS transitions on height 117 - **Line chart**: `` or `` with stroke-dasharray animation 118 - **Donut chart**: `` with stroke-dasharray/stroke-dashoffset 119 - **Sparkline**: tiny `` in KPI cards 120 121 ### Best Practices 122 - Use CSS Grid with `auto-fit` and `minmax()` for responsive cards 123 - Subtle card shadows, no borders 124 - Color-code positive (green) and negative (red) changes 125 - Tooltips on hover for data points 126 - Auto-refresh indicator (even if static — sells the "live" feel) 127 128 --- 129 130 ## Flowchart / Diagram 131 132 ### Approach 133 Use SVG for the diagram. Position nodes with CSS Grid or absolute positioning within an SVG viewBox. 134 135 ### Node Types 136 ```svg 137 138 139 140 141 142 143 144 145 ``` 146 147 ### Connection Lines 148 - Use `` with cubic bezier curves for smooth connections 149 - Arrow markers: `` element with `` arrowhead 150 - Elbow connectors for orthogonal layouts 151 152 ### Best Practices 153 - Left-to-right or top-to-bottom flow 154 - Consistent node sizes 155 - Labels centered in nodes 156 - Color-code different paths (success=green, error=red) 157 - Keep it simple: max 15-20 nodes before splitting into sub-diagrams 158 159 --- 160 161 ## Timeline 162 163 ### Layout Options 164 1. **Vertical** — line down the center, events alternate left/right 165 2. **Horizontal** — scrollable timeline for fewer events 166 3. **Compact** — single column with dots and lines 167 168 ### Vertical Timeline Pattern 169 ``` 170 ┌──────────┐ 171 │ Event 1 │──── ● 172 └──────────┘ │ 173 │ 174 ● ────┌──────────┐ 175 │ Event 2 │ 176 └──────────┘ 177 │ 178 ┌──────────┐ │ 179 │ Event 3 │──── ● 180 └──────────┘ 181 ``` 182 183 ### Best Practices 184 - Alternating sides for visual balance 185 - Dates prominently displayed 186 - Color/icon differentiation for event types 187 - Scroll-triggered entrance animations 188 - "Now" marker for roadmaps 189 190 --- 191 192 ## Comparison 193 194 ### Layout Options 195 1. **Side-by-side cards** — 2-3 options in columns 196 2. **Feature matrix** — rows = features, columns = options, checkmarks/values 197 3. **Before/After** — split screen 198 199 ### Feature Matrix Pattern 200 - Sticky header row 201 - Alternating row backgrounds 202 - ✓ / ✗ icons (SVG) instead of text 203 - Highlight recommended option with accent border/badge 204 205 ### Best Practices 206 - Max 4 comparison columns (more = overwhelming) 207 - Highlight key differentiators 208 - Use icons for quick scanning 209 - Color-code to guide toward recommended option (subtle, not pushy) 210 211 --- 212 213 ## Data Visualization 214 215 ### Chart Types (all SVG-based) 216 - **Bar**: vertical or horizontal, grouped or stacked 217 - **Line**: single or multi-series, area fills 218 - **Pie/Donut**: max 6 segments, label percentages 219 - **Scatter**: for correlations, size for third dimension 220 - **Heatmap**: grid of colored cells 221 222 ### SVG Chart Essentials 223 - Always include axes with labels 224 - Grid lines: subtle (`stroke: #eee`, `stroke-dasharray: 4`) 225 - Legend: positioned consistently (top-right or bottom) 226 - Responsive viewBox: `viewBox="0 0 600 400"` with `preserveAspectRatio` 227 - Animate on load: stroke-dasharray for lines, scaleY for bars 228 229 ### Best Practices 230 - Lead with the insight, not the data 231 - Annotate key data points directly on the chart 232 - Don't use 3D effects 233 - Start y-axis at 0 for bar charts (line charts can break this rule) 234 - Max 5-7 data series per chart 235 236 --- 237 238 ## One-Pager 239 240 ### Structure 241 - Hero section with headline + subtext 242 - 3-4 content sections 243 - Clear CTA or conclusion 244 - Max viewport: feels complete without scrolling (or minimal scroll) 245 246 ### Best Practices 247 - Large hero text (48px+) 248 - Icon + text pairs for features 249 - Centered layout, max-width 960px 250 - Professional but not boring — one bold design choice 251 - Works as a screenshot/PDF 252 253 --- 254 255 ## Mind Map 256 257 ### Approach 258 - Central node with radiating branches 259 - SVG with `` curved connections 260 - Color-code branches by category 261 - Nodes expand on click (optional interactivity) 262 263 ### Layout Algorithm (simplified) 264 - Center node at viewBox center 265 - First-level nodes in a circle around center 266 - Second-level nodes branch outward from their parent 267 - Use polar coordinates for positioning 268 269 ### Best Practices 270 - Max 2-3 levels deep for readability 271 - Curved, organic-looking connections (bezier) 272 - Node size reflects importance 273 - Hover to highlight a branch and dim others 274 275 --- 276 277 ## Kanban Board 278 279 ### Structure 280 ```html 281

cat << 'PYEOF' > /app/output/render_poster.py
import asyncio
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

async def render_poster():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        browser = await p.chromium.launch()
        page = await browser.new_page()
        
        # Set viewport to A1 portrait at 96 DPI
        await page.set_viewport_size({"width": 2234, "height": 3175})
        
        # Load the HTML file
        await page.goto("file:///app/output/poster.html", wait_until="networkidle")
        
        # Wait for fonts to load and animations to settle
        await page.wait_for_timeout(2000)
        
        # Take screenshot
        await page.screenshot(
            path="/app/output/final_poster.png",
            type="png",
            full_page=False
        )
        
        await browser.close()
        print("Poster rendered successfully to /app/output/final_poster.png")

asyncio.run(render_poster())
PYEOF

import asyncio
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

async def render_poster():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        browser = await p.chromium.launch()
        page = await browser.new_page()
        
        # Set viewport to A1 portrait at 96 DPI
        await page.set_viewport_size({"width": 2234, "height": 3175})
        
        # Load the HTML file
        await page.goto("file:///app/output/poster.html", wait_until="networkidle")
        
        # Force dark theme
        await page.evaluate("""
            document.documentElement.className = 'theme-dark';
            localStorage.setItem('viz-theme', 'dark');
        """)
        
        # Wait for fonts to load and animations to settle
        await page.wait_for_timeout(2000)
        
        # Take screenshot
        await page.screenshot(
            path="/app/output/final_poster.png",
            type="png",
            full_page=False
        )
        
        await browser.close()
        print("Poster rendered successfully to /app/output/final_poster.png")

asyncio.run(render_poster())

steps.message:
The A1 portrait poster has been successfully created and exported. Here's a summary of what was delivered:

## Output
- **Final poster:** `/app/output/final_poster.png`
- **Dimensions:** 2234 × 3175 px (A1 portrait at 96 DPI)
- **Format:** Single self-contained PNG image

## Design Highlights

**Visual Style:**
- Deep navy/charcoal background (`#0f172a`) with warm amber (`#f59e0b`) and coral (`#f97316`) accents
- Clean, modern typography using Inter font with bold hierarchical sizing
- Subtle radial gradient atmosphere for depth

**Content Structure (top to bottom):**
1. **Header** — Bold title "The State of Global Education" with subtitle
2. **Progress Arc** — Dramatic side-by-side comparison: `< 1 in 5` (1800) → `> 4 in 5` (today) with narrative
3. **Hero Stat** — **244 million** children out of school as the visually dominant centerpiece, with breakdown (60M primary / 184M secondary)
4. **Quality Comparison** — Bold side-by-side cards: `< 3 years` (poorest countries, red) vs `10+ years` (rich countries, green)
5. **Bottom Row** — Learning crisis (`< 20%` reading proficiency) and gender gap closure (Primary/Secondary/Tertiary)
6. **Footer** — Key takeaway + data source attribution

**Key Priorities Met:**
- ✅ The "progress vs. gaps" contrast is central to the narrative
- ✅ **244 million** is the largest, most visually dominant element
- ✅ The `< 3 years` vs `10+ years` comparison is immediately graspable via bold side-by-side cards
- ✅ Data-forward yet engaging tone, accessible to general public
